idiom_name: interface-checked no-op literal object + strictNullChecks with ?. / ??
implementation_notes: With strictNullChecks the compiler distinguishes Logger from Logger | undefined, so absence is visible in the type and handled with ?. and ?? rather than by substituting a collaborator; when callers must call unconditionally, the null object is a single frozen literal that satisfies the interface (const nullLogger: Logger = Object.freeze({ log() {} })) used as a constructor default. Because interfaces are structural, the compiler verifies that the null object implements every member - the omission that would fail only at run time in JavaScript is a compile error here. Prefer the nullable type when absence must be actioned; prefer the null object when it must not.
pitfalls: With strictNullChecks off - or with any/! in the call path - the null object is a convention rather than a checked invariant, and logger! reintroduces the null-dereference risk the type system removed.
Types are erased at run time: the interface guarantees the null object has the members, but nothing stops a null from JSON, a DI container or plain JavaScript reaching the call.

Structural typing can make an unrelated empty object the null object: an interface with only optional members is satisfied by {}, so such an 'implementation' can appear without anyone deciding it should.
